daily.title: Marco Rubio visits India this week, with a visit to the world's largest oil refinery topping the agenda
daily.summary: A visit to India this week by Washington's top diplomat will skip New Delhi and instead include the world's largest oil refinery that processes massive amounts of Russian crude. Is Trump looking for a new deal?

daily.title: 'We don't have to wait for others to support us': Myanmar refugees find hope in Thailand's work program
daily.summary: A year ago, Thailand granted long-staying refugees from Myanmar the right to work legally. Refugees and rights groups welcome the move but say the program's first year has exposed significant shortcomings.

daily.title: UN food program cuts aid to 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza
daily.summary: Amid funding shortages, the World Food Program has said it is being forced to reduce necessary aid. Over two-thirds of Palestinians in Gaza are facing acute hunger, according to the agency.

daily.title: From delivery driver to global fame: A Korean writer's journey
daily.summary: You Yeong-Gwang's The Rainfall Market tells the story of a mysterious, hidden shop that only opens when it rains. For a debut novel by an unknown author, it was a massive success.

daily.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
daily.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

daily.title: Greece: At least 12 die in migrant drownings overnight
daily.summary: Authorities say 12 people, including an infant, have drowned in Greek waters in two separate incidents overnight. Another 22 people were rescued. A search-and-rescue operation is ongoing.

daily.title: Australian MP seriously hurt in suspected car attack
daily.summary: Helen Haines, an independent federal lawmaker, has been struck by a car in what Australia's prime minister has called an apparent attack.

daily.title: Ukraine got 'no warning' of Russian ballistic strikes, Zelenskyy says
daily.summary: Massive strikes overnight hit the capital Kyiv, and damaged power stations, killing at least one person and cutting power to hundreds of thousands.

daily.title: West Bank: Israel arrests 10 suspects over settler attacks on US journalist, European diplomats
daily.summary: Israeli police made the arrests following attacks on a US journalist and European diplomats in the occupied West Bank. Israeli human rights group Yesh Din has reported at least 170 settler attacks since September 27.

daily.title: Deepfakes, bots and distrust: How AI is shaping Israel's election
daily.summary: For the first time, AI is playing a major role in Israel's elections. Observers warn that deepfakes, bots and influence campaigns could sway voters.

daily.title: Germany news: Berlin conference seeks to drum up investment
daily.summary: The "Invest in Germany Summit" is set to kick off in Berlin as the government looks to fill gaps in public funding. DW has more.

daily.title: India news: CJP alleges 'deliberate' delay in leaders' release
daily.summary: CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were due to be released on Sunday. The judge in the case has recused himself after claiming that he was threatened. DW has more.

daily.title: Brazil: Lula, Bolsonaro clash in heated presidential debate
daily.summary: The candidates traded barbs, including over Bolsonaro's ties to US President Donald Trump in their first debate, days before the October 25 election runoff.

daily.title: Emmanuel Macron slams 'failures' over protest unrest in France but refuses his interior minister's resignation
daily.summary: France's president has refused the resignation of his interior minister, who says police "lost control" during protests that turned violent at the weekend. France's PM has called for limited curfews around the country.

daily.title: What Earth's sixth mass extinction event means for humans
daily.summary: Human activity is driving plants and animals to extinction at an unprecedented rate. As countries meet in Armenia to discuss ways to reverse nature loss, DW reveals how declining biodiversity is already harming people.

daily.title: Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv makes emergency landing after bomb threat
daily.summary: An Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna made an emergency landing in Bulgaria after a bomb threat was reported near the Bulgarian-Romanian border. A MiG-29 fighter jet escorted the plane.

daily.title: Trump defends Russia sanctions waivers, accuses Zelenskyy of 'prolonging war'
daily.summary: The US president again accused his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war. The remarks come amid renewed tensions over US policy toward Moscow, including waiving some sanctions.

daily.title: Canada: Fire at Alberta military Base kills four, leaves 19 in critical condition
daily.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says a "serious incident" sparked a major fire at on Alberta military base. Four people have died, 39 are in hospital and at least 19 are in critical condition.

daily.title: Ebola: Kenya cases rise to 8, spreads to 8th Congo province
daily.summary: A senior health official in Kenya said there have now been eight Ebola infections in the country, while in DR Congo the disease has spread to an eighth province.

daily.title: Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama ignores calls to resign amid violent clashes
daily.summary: Anti-government protesters continued calls for Edi Rama to step down as violent clashes between demonstrators and police persisted.

daily.title: France: Young voters blase about Glucksmann's Socialists
daily.summary: Raphael Glucksmann wants to lead France's Socialists to power without working with the left-populist Jean-Luc Melenchon, who is particularly popular with young voters. How can the center-left candidate win them over?

weekly.title: Is Germany's eight-hour workday under threat?
weekly.summary: Would you work 12 hours straight? The CDU/CSU and SPD are locked in a dispute over reforms to the Working Hours Act. Workplace flexibility, collective bargaining agreements and worker protection rules are at stake.

weekly.title: How reliant is Ukraine on the US-controlled Starlink internet service?
weekly.summary: Kyiv keeps issuing warnings that the satellite internet system Starlink is being restricted in Ukraine. How dependent is the country on the system, and what would happen if it went down?

weekly.title: Populist Czech PM Babis goes empty-handed in Senate elections
weekly.summary: Opposition parties still control the Czech Senate, in a major blow to Prime Minister Andrej Babis' and his governing coalition.

weekly.title: How big is Russia's threat against Germany?
weekly.summary: Experts believe that, so far, Germany has been ill-prepared — both militarily and mentally — for Russian provocations. They also warn against the idea that ending support for Ukraine would make Germany safer.

weekly.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
weekly.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

weekly.title: Russia wants blackout in Ukraine as winter comes — Zelenskyy
weekly.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says Russia is trying to cut electricity and heating to civilians ahead of winter. He also called the US president's waiver of new sanctions on Moscow a boost for Vladimir Putin.

weekly.title: France: Protesters clash with police in nationwide protests, amid rising social polarization
weekly.summary: Unrest broke out in parts of France as students, trade unionists and Yellow Vest activists took to the streets to protest high prices and inequality. Police arrested over 1,000 people amid chaotic scenes.

weekly.title: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy speaks at EU summit amid spat with Donald Trump
weekly.summary: EU leaders reaffirmed support for Ukraine at the Brussels summit. But souring relations with the US over Russia and Starlink and a big hole in the budget will make for a difficult winter for Ukraine.

weekly.title: Hijab ban at schools in Azerbaijan: What's behind the rare wave of protests?
weekly.summary: Girls wearing headscarves have been turned away from schools in Azerbaijan, triggering unusual protests involving children. The government rules do not mention hijabs. Why are schools enforcing unwritten rules?

weekly.title: The Bundestag has debated the genocide Germany carried out in Namibia a century ago. But will it spur progress on addressing colonial crimes?
weekly.summary: Opposition parties have forced a debate in the Bundestag on the early-20th-century genocide Germany carried out in Namibia. Will this finally spur progress in addressing colonial crimes?

weekly.title: Albania: Students demand political change and resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama
weekly.summary: Empty lecture halls, burning buildings and demands for change: Albanian students are spearheading a protest movement that has become the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Edi Rama in years.

weekly.title: The EU wants an AI revolution. But on whose terms?
weekly.summary: As the US and China race ahead, the European Union seeks to boost its economy with AI. Can it compete while protecting workers, safety and the climate?

weekly.title: Italy cuts air traffic in half amid data transmission issue
weekly.summary: Citing problems with the data transmission network, Italian authorities have drastically reduced the volume of flights in their airspace. The ENAV authority ruled out malicious activity and said flights remained safe.

weekly.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
weekly.summary: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.

weekly.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
weekly.summary: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

weekly.title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy
weekly.summary: Formula One will return to Africa for the first time since 1993. There is concern Rwanda are using it as another sportswashing opportunity, but there is also hope the event's legacy can impact wider African society.

weekly.title: Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
weekly.summary: Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against corruption charges.

weekly.title: EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget
weekly.summary: EU leaders meeting in Brussels will examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. But they will also be looking to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of some major elections next year.

weekly.title: Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing
weekly.summary: Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.

weekly.title: Resignation of Bärbel Bas shines light on harsh era of German politics
weekly.summary: German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas has stepped down, citing her need to grieve a loved one and leave behind the harsh realities of government. So how did German politics get so heated?

weekly.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
weekly.summary: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

weekly.title: Thousands of German gamblers could sue for their money back
weekly.summary: German gamblers may finally be able to beat the house, thanks to new court rulings in the EU and in Germany. The decisions could help gambling addicts — but the legal road might be difficult.

weekly.title: Germany news: Train station alcohol ban comes into force
weekly.summary: Consuming alcohol is no longer permitted at train stations in Germany, to improve the lot of travelers and staff alike. Coalition talks are restarting in Berlin, and an inmate is loose in Essen.

weekly.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
weekly.summary: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

weekly.title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
weekly.summary: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?

weekly.title: Manchester City, the UAE and the UK's OM in a political tangle
weekly.summary: Nearly 20 years after arriving in England, Manchester City's UAE owners could exit amid cheating charges. That would pose a challenge for a city — and prime minister — closely tied to Abu Dhabi.

weekly.title: Nord Stream trial opens in Germany, defense seeks dismissal
weekly.summary: Serhii Kuznietsov is accused of attacking civilian infrastructure in the 2022 sabotage of the Russian gas pipeline to Germany. His lawyers called Nord Stream a military target, and said their client is sworn to secrecy.

weekly.title: Germany's far-right AfD forges a pro-Russia alliance with the BSW
weekly.summary: In Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD and BSW are joining forces to push for negotiations with Moscow. What is driving this rapprochement?

weekly.title: Albania: Fire at Education Ministry as students protest
weekly.summary: Riot police deployed in the Albanian capital Tirana on the second day of student protests. The sudden outbreak seemed at least somewhat reminiscent of the widespread demos in France courting international attention.

weekly.title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
weekly.summary: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.

weekly.title: Nord Stream: Germany puts suspected Ukrainian pipeline saboteur on trial
weekly.summary: A Ukrainian citizen faces court in Hamburg, accused of attacking the Nord Stream gas pipelines in 2022. It raises questions about Kyiv's possible role in the explosions. German support for Ukraine is also under scrutiny.

weekly.title: Fact check: Misleading graph about alleged Russian bot activity
weekly.summary: Did attacks on Russian data centers reduce bot activity around Germany's AfD? A viral graph claims they did. But it contains significant inconsistencies and provides no evidence to support the claim.

weekly.title: Do non-German nationals commit more crimes than Germans?
weekly.summary: People without German passports appear more frequently in German police crime statistics than German nationals. A new study explains why.

weekly.title: FIFPRO report highlights growing pains in women's football
weekly.summary: Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for better structures globally.

weekly.title: The hidden treasure in discarded wearable and fast tech
weekly.summary: Sales of fast tech like mini fans and disposable e-vapes, as well as wearable health tech such as heart monitors and smartwatches are soaring. They're creating a new e-waste problem but are full of hidden treasure.

weekly.title: Ukraine allies in Poland after Starlink sabotage, Trump diesel deal
weekly.summary: Germany's Johann Wadephul said hybrid plots like the Starlink fire showed Europe was "in Russia's crosshairs." The UK's Ed Miliband said Trump's Russian diesel deal led to a "very difficult few days" diplomatically.

weekly.title: Ukraine and the US: What's next after Trump's diesel deal with Russia?
weekly.summary: Donald Trump plans to allow the purchase of Russian diesel, drawing criticism at home and abroad. What is behind the US president's decision and what should Ukraine do next? DW spoke with experts.

weekly.title: Critics warn of espionage risks as Slovakia restores military-diplomatic representation with Russia
weekly.summary: Slovakia is restoring military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since 2022. The government has defended the move but critics warn of espionage risks and further damage to trust within NATO.

weekly.title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
weekly.summary: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s," continuing the country’s investment in international sport.

weekly.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
weekly.summary: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

weekly.title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'
weekly.summary: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.

weekly.title: What is holding back Cyprus's Schengen ambitions?
weekly.summary: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Yet questions relating to the island's division and British military bases could still complicate its path to Europe's border-free travel zone.

weekly.title: Germany: Labor Minister's resignation puts a spotlight on cracks within the government
weekly.summary: Following the sudden resignation of Bärbel Bas as Labor Minister and co-chair of the Social Democratic Party, accusations are flying in Chancellor Merz's coalition government.

weekly.title: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
weekly.summary: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
